utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. But indeed nobody called me up for any kind of exercises or anything at the 4th Detachment. I know, as a matter of fact, that Radovan Antic was commander of the 4th Detachment but I was never called up. Although, I had been issued a weapon earlier. MR. DI FAZIO: Is this an appropriate time, if Your Honours please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And the proceedings will continue at 14.15. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.45 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, you can continue. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, you were issued with a high-powered automatic weapon as part of your membership -- as a result of your membership of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given a uniform?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend training?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that the commander of the 4th Detachment was Mr. Radovan Antic.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him well enough to speak to on a personal and social level?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that on the 16th -- on the night of the 16th and 17th, the town came under attack and armed paramilitaries took over government in the town. You knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You knew that on the night of the 16th and 17th the town had come under attack from paramilitaries, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that on the night of the 16th and 17th there had been the sound of explosions and gunfire, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had heard explosions and also gunshots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that this was completely out of the ordinary, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's said -- I withdraw that. It seemed to you, did it not, that the town was under attack?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I didn't really know that the town was under attack. I had heard that there was an exchange of fire, but I didn't really know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seemed to you that the town might be under attack and at the very, very least a serious situation was developing in the town; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: The situation was unusual, but I didn't really think that it would be under attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make --

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: That the town could ever be under attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the 17th wore on, during the day you became aware of all of these things, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the 17th wore on, you became aware that the town had been under attack and that a very serious situation was developing in the town.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I knew that something unusual was going on, but that the city was under attack or that an extraordinary situation was in place, I did not understand that at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent the night with your neighbours in a corridor calming each other down, didn't you, the night of the 16th and 17th?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That at the very least, surely, indicates that an unusual and dangerous situation was developing.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you not consider in those circumstances that it was your duty to report to the 4th Detachment, or at the very least contact the 4th Detachment to see if your services as a member of the 4th Detachment were required?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. Nobody called me, and I did not report myself to the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling the Trial Chamber that between the 16th -- well, indeed from the 16th -- the night of the 16th and 17th onwards you never received any communication from the command of the 4th Detachment regarding mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. Absolutely no communication whatsoever, no one called me, no one gave me an order. I was absolutely isolated, kept isolated from the events that were going on in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: From the 4th Detachment. I'm sorry. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why you were kept isolated?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Believe me that I really do not know and I never asked either. I suppose that the reason for this was that because I was a news person and that's why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I understand your reasoning, Mr. Antic. In fact, you were aware, weren't you, that other members of the 4th Detachment were responding to mobilisation orders taking up positions on the Sava and the Bosna and also collecting weapons?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I did not know where they were deployed, but I did know that they had answered the call-up to join the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there may be a problem with the way your answer was translated. Do you mean to say that they had answered the mobilisation call to spring into action? Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th, on the 18th, on the 19th of April, 1992, did you personally become aware of the 4th Detachment mobilising, taking up positions on the Bosna and Sava River, and participating in the collection of weapons? Did you become aware --

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. No, I did not become aware of it because I went to the radio station on the 18th, and this is where I spent my time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Did you ever walk on down to the Sava or the Bosna and have a walk along the river at any time in those three days?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't dare, because there was an exchange of fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that the 4th Detachment was involved in the exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No, I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any members of the 4th Detachment come to your home or the home of your neighbours looking for weapons? Did you see any of that, at your home or your apartment building or indeed in your street or indeed in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. I believed [as interpreted] downtown in a building on the fourth floor, and during those days that you are mentioning I never noticed anybody coming to collect weapons. Nobody came to my door, anyways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the days following the outbreak of hostilities in Bosanski Samac, did it ever occur to you to go and see your commanders and ask them if you had any role to fulfil as a member of the 4th Detachment, any activity that perhaps you should undertake with your automatic weapon that had been issued to you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. It never even occurred to me to go and see what was happening over there because nobody called me, and aside from that, I was a member of the 4th Detachment but I was not engaged in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber what -- what it means to be a member of the 4th Detachment but not engaged in it. Can you explain that for them, please.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: If they had ever called me, I would have surely answered the call or the call-up because I know that the 4th Detachment was such a unit in which members of all ethnicities were involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me this: Do you agree that there was an outbreak of hostilities, there was fighting going on in Bosanski Samac in the days and weeks following?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. Thank you. And tell me, did the 4th Detachment have any role to play -- to play in that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Since I was not an active member of the 4th Detachment during that period of time, I believe that the 4th Detachment had the task to alleviate tensions, to make sure that there is no conflict, armed conflict. That's according to my own belief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I put to you, Mr. Antic, that you're not telling the truth and that the fact of the matter is that you know very well that there was a mobilisation order, that there was an order to seize weapons, and that there was an order requiring members of the 4th Detachment to take up positions on the Sava and the Bosna and that you were exempted from those requirements by your work at the radio station.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the radio station. It was your work at the radio station that saved you from having to participate in those actions of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I suppose so. But let me tell you, Mr. Prosecutor, I have always tried -- I always tried to tell the truth and I certainly wouldn't lie here in front of this very Honourable Trial Chamber. All my life I wrote the truth. I was five times brought before the courts and I always won my case. I had problems during the war because I always told the truth. I just want to tell you that I can only make a mistake, but I will never say intentionally something that is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I put to you that your exemption from these activities that were undertaken by the 4th Detachment was well known to the command of the 4th Detachment and that they were instrumental in exempting you so you could go and work in this civilian authority, namely the information service and the radio station.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I can only suppose that that's the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Pasaga Tihic, he had in fact stopped working at the radio station about a year before and at the time was working in a company called elektrodistribucija, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to the radio station, you already had -- there were already employees who were working there, including Mr. Cordasevic?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't Cordasevic a reporter at the -- at the radio station?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: He was a reporter, but he came only when I called him, because I was the first one to get there and he was the first one I called and he came immediately to the radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What I meant was that you -- prior to the 16th, you had already a staff in existence working.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. We'll leave that topic and move on to the employment of -- the use of Pasaga Tihic's services. First of all, on the 18th of April, Dr. Blagoje Simic called you and instructed you to get the radio station up and operating. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. Stevan Todorovic was the one who gave me the instructions, according to the orders of Blagoje Simic. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it the case that on the 18th of April you were telephoned by Blagoje Simic, president of the Crisis Staff, and told that the radio had to be put back in order and must start broadcasting programmes?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: That is correct. But I said already that it was his order but carried out through other people; that is to say, Todorovic and Simeon Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forget about what happened later. I'm only interested in the telephone call. It was the voice of Dr. Blagoje Simic. He was on the other end of the telephone, and he gave you the instructions to get the radio station up and running.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of my testimony I already said that a voice called me from the Crisis Staff. That person did not introduce himself, and even when I asked him who it was, he didn't want to tell me who it was, but he said that Dr. Blagoje Simic, the president of the Crisis Staff, ordered that the radio station should be up and operational.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever told anyone, particularly towards the end of last year, that it was Dr. Blagoje Simic who telephoned you and told you that the radio had to be put back in order and start broadcasting programmes? Have you ever told anyone that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having ever told that to anyone, but I said that through an intermediary, through a person, he had ordered that the radio station should be put back in order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time that you were asked to recall the telephone call that got you to go and repair the radio station?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, between 1200 hours and 1300 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. When -- when were you asked by anyone to cast your mind back, to think about the events of 1992 and explain what happened as far as this phone call on the 18th is concerned?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was who telephoned you on the 18th? Do you know who it was on the other end of the line?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I suppose that it was Simeon Simic, but I'm not certain of this. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment, please, while I confer with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm well aware of the ruling that you have now made absolutely clear on two occasions, and I don't intend to revisit that. I understand that perfectly well, and I've heard you again this morning. However, I propose to attempt to refresh this witness's memory by showing him a portion of the paragraphs that we -- that we know are not -- not contained. That, of course, is done with a view to refreshing his memory. It is not done with a view to attacking credit. So I thought I'd make that clear that that's my proposal, and I seek a -- a ruling from you as to whether or not I am permitted to do so because of the -- for obvious reasons. So that's the purpose, merely to show it to him to refresh memory, not to attack credit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Di Fazio. The Trial Chamber will not allow that because -- MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- it still remains that paragraphs which are struck off cannot be resurrected in any other way. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well. Thank you, Your Honours, for providing that guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: As you are still cross-examining, you can put it to the witness, because from the point of view of your cross-examination it seems to be -- it seems that there is a contradiction. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Within the evidence of the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Well, I'll -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever told Mr. Pisarevic that it was the president of the Crisis Staff, Blagoje Simic, who contacted you by phone and gave instructions for the resurrection of the radio station?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain to this Honourable Trial Chamber this event. I just wish to say the following: Dr. Blagoje Simic had ordered directly that the radio be put back in order, but not him directly. Through his employees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Through his associates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. How do you know that it was the order of Blagoje Simic that initiated this -- that initiated this repair job at the radio station?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I will repeat my answer that I already gave previously. The phone call said that the Crisis Staff or Dr. Blagoje Simic gave me those instructions. I don't know how else to explain this to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, at about the time of this telephone conversation, Pasaga Tihic was in custody, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I didn't know it, actually. I was not particularly interested in it either. I only found out about it when I got to the radio station that Pasaga Tihic was in custody, but only when I got to the radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find out at the radio station that Pasaga Tihic was in custody?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I already said that I came there and I wanted some associates, people who would work there. I needed a technician, somebody who would be able to operate the radio. I already said that the technician was a Croat from the village of Prud. I couldn't reach him. But then I recall that Pasaga used to work at the radio station a year before that or a year and a half before that. I'm not sure. I knew that Pasaga was an excellent technician and this is why I called him, because I knew that the mid-wave transmitter was not operational and this is why I asked Stevan Todorovic to release him so that he can come and help me operate the radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as part of the process of getting Pasaga Tihic released, did you speak to Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it the case that since you didn't have any technicians, you told Blagoje Simic, who in turn told you to speak to Stevan Todorovic, because he had arrested Pasaga Tihic?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the sequence was Blagoje Simic first, he tells you that Pasaga Tihic is in custody, and he puts you on to Stevan Todorovic. Then you speak to Todorovic, and Tihic is then released and comes and works at the radio station. That's the sequence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact sequence of events, but I believe that that was the right sequence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And you would have had to telephone Blagoje Simic at the Crisis Staff in order to get to him and raise this issue of Pasaga Tihic coming to work at the radio station.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I already said earlier that I got the information that all the contacts in future should be carried out through and with the people from the Crisis Staff, Simeunovic and Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Simeon Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that he was a member of the Crisis Staff and at a time when you knew he was a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that at that time he was a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The result was that Pasaga Tihic was brought to you at the radio station in the custody of two policemen.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thereafter, you had to take him to report to the police station on a twice-daily basis?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Todorovic kept a close eye on his work at the radio station, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you continuing at the radio station in -- as part of your normal duties, the normal work that you had done prior to the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you got a salary?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much was Pasaga Tihic paid?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: He got something, but I can't remember how much. I can't remember how much I got either by way of a salary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. One of the reasons Pasaga Tihic was able to stay on at the radio station was the fact that he was training another man, Goran Bosic or Bosic. I'm not sure how you pronounce it.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was stringing out that training process, wasn't he, so he didn't have to go into custody?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did the training process come to an end?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: This is the way it was: The training took about a month, perhaps a bit more than a month. And then Stevan Todorovic called me nervously, asking me whether this training process had been finished by then, and I said that it had and Goran Bosic took over as technician and then they came yet again and took Pasaga Tihic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that the training process coming to an end could consign Goran Bosic -- or Bosic to whatever fate Todorovic had in store for him?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I tried to keep both technicians at the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, I misled you. My question should have been: You knew that the training process coming to an end would consign Pasaga Tihic to whatever fate Todorovic had in store for him?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Well, to tell you quite honestly, that was not my job. I wanted to have two technicians at the radio, as I had had before. I needed both Goran Bosic and Pasaga Tihic. However, I was not asked about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simo Zaric was a man who was well known in the community in 1992; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He often gave public speeches?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. And he often was on the radio talking about the 4th Detachment, wasn't he? In fact, on one occasion, at least, he spoke on radio with Nikolic, didn't he, Colonel Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I really don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were working at the radio station in early 1992 though, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: 1992, yes. Yes. Not the beginning, though, but throughout. Before 1992 and after 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during 1992?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You knew, didn't you, that Simo Zaric was the assistant commander in the 4th Detachment for intelligence, reconnaissance, morale, and information?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I knew, but I really did not know which position he actually held. I really didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the public face of the 4th Detachment, wasn't he? He was the man who spoke on behalf of the 4th Detachment publicly most often.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Not on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the man -- he was the public face of the 4th Detachment. He was the man who spoke on behalf of the 4th Detachment publicly in places other than the radio.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that either, really, because I did not have contact with the 4th Detachment, although I was a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that he was never on the radio speaking about the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember - and I was on the radio all the time - he really wasn't, except for that tape when they all appeared together on TV Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say, don't you, that one of the reasons Simo Zaric didn't come to the radio to speak was that he was banned by Todorovic? Is that a fair assessment of your position?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this ban placed?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Soon when the radio station's programme began. But I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. It's a long time ago. But was it in a matter of days after the 16th, or are we talking weeks after the 16th or months?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: A few weeks after the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for a few weeks initially Simo Zaric was not banned and could gain access to the radio station.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: He could, but he was not present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your position is that he never once spoke on the radio, no one in Bosanski Samac ever heard his voice after the 16th of April on any occasion or on any topic?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you're aware, he never made any moves to try and get to speak on the radio. He didn't contact you or Simeon Simic or Cordasevic or anyone else to try and get radio time?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Simo Zaric did not address me, and I don't know about others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you're not aware of him ever having contacted anyone with a view to getting radio time?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Todorovic inform the radio station of the ban on Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: He informed me personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he give --

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, he made a threat that if that were to happen, that he'd hand me over to the Ustashas. I have to say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you explain to him that Mr. Zaric hadn't been seen near the radio station, had never contacted anyone with a view to getting radio time?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I did not explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Todorovic just come out of the blue and say to you that Zaric was banned?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic would barge into the radio any time during the day or night. He would make threats, and he would be the one creating the radio programme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was the duty of the radio to inform the public, inform the citizens of Bosanski Samac and the municipality, of important developments in the town, important developments that the civilian administration was working on, and also on military matters.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That included reporting on the activity of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Everything that came and everything that came as an order is what we broadcast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You broadcast, didn't you, on activities of the 4th Detachment and its later incarnation as the 5th Battalion in the Army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I do not remember that anything special was broadcast from the 4th Detachment, that any kind of need was expressed for that or that anything like that had been asked for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was radio silence, so to speak, on the activities of the detachment that had been set up to defend the town; is that what you're saying? The very military unit that is charged with responsibility of protecting the town, no one heard anything about its activities over the radio in the weeks following the takeover?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I cannot make any comments on what I don't know. I don't go into the reasons and I'm not aware of the reasons. I am not competent to say why it is this way rather than that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was nothing over the radio in the weeks following the 16th of April of what the 4th Detachment was doing?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown D28/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Does the Prosecution have a copy of the exhibit? MR. DI FAZIO: We do. I think we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That can be shown to the witness, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- lend a copy. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, that -- that's a statement prepared on behalf of the 4th Detachment. You're familiar with that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier this morning, I believe -- do you recall the statement now?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I said that there was an announcement, but I said that I did not remember its contents. That's what I said earlier on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. But that's -- I suggest to you that that's the statement. And in fact, that statement was read out several times over the radio, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric was interviewed by officers of the OTP on April the 2nd, 1998 and in the course of discussing events in Bosanski Samac said that the statement was read out three times over the radio. Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I told you that I really do not remember the contents. I also said that this statement was on the radio once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You know that the 4th Detachment collected weapons in Bosanski Samac on the 17th and 18th of April, 1992, collected weapons from the citizenry?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I've already said that I really don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Over 30.000 people live in Bosanski Samac, don't they -- then lived in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there are lots and lots of apartments in buildings and lots of houses standing by themselves on blocks of land.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: 30.000 was the population of the entire municipality. The town itself had a population of about 6.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that lots of proclamations and orders were read out over the radio in the days immediately following the 16th and 17th of April. For example, the state of emergency, curfew, and so on.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree that if the 4th Detachment was to go about the task of collecting weapons, orders for that or information about that over the radio would have facilitated their task?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to this question, because it leads the witness to speculation. How can he know whether this would have facilitated their task or not? MR. DI FAZIO: I'll withdraw it. I'll withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The radio station -- the radio station was called Radio Samac before the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Radio Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it called after the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Then it was called Radio Bosanski Samac too. Later on the usual way of putting it was Radio Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that Todorovic was responsible for censoring of news. You agree with that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't just nod your head --

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I need your -- sorry, I wasn't being rude. I need your voice so that it's recorded and so it goes onto the transcript. That's the only reason I make the -- I want an actual answer.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I said yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the massacre of 15 or 16 Croats at Crkvina was a matter that was extremely well known throughout the town; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know how many people were in town, but I know that I heard about that piece of news a month and a half later. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown his statement. Do you have your statement there? He's got it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at paragraphs -- paragraph 26 of your statement. Paragraph 26, third sentence, "It was absolutely no secret that a crime was committed in Crkvina in which 16 prisoners were killed, nor that there were Croats imprisoned in the secondary school and the TO building." So in your own words, it was absolutely no secret. You agree with that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean. What do you mean it was no secret?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean that it was extremely well known that 16 or so Croats had been slaughtered in a warehouse at Crkvina, 6 or 7 kilometres just outside of Bosanski Samac. It was well known in the town, it was known to you, and it was well known in the town almost immediately after the event. That's a correct scenario, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know how well known it was almost immediately after the event. I found out about it a month and a half later, perhaps a month later or a month and a half later. That's really the way it was. I have no reason to tell you anything but the way it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So a month later. And a month later it was well known throughout the town that the slaughter had happened.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was absolutely no point in keeping it from the people; it was already well known throughout the town. Now, given that situation and given your evidence just before the break that you were endeavouring to inform the public objectively, did you not consider it appropriate to report upon this particular massacre?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I was the editor-in-chief at that time, but I found out very late. You know that there is no more perishable goods than news. If it is not carried the next day, then it's no use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So Crkvina was -- the massacre of 16 people at Crkvina was old news a month later; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I am trying to say that really so much time had gone by that I had assumed that everybody had heard about that, and that kind of news is carried immediately, as soon as something like that happens. Not only that, but any other piece of news, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or anyone at the radio station propose, at least, running some sort of story on this massacre, discuss the possibility?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So no one was able to stop you from printing any story. It wasn't even discussed -- sorry, not printing any story. Broadcasting any story on the massacre. It wasn't even discussed. That possibility wasn't even discussed.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Again, I wish to say that after a month or after a month and a half - I don't know exactly - I heard about that particular piece of news, I personally. There was no point. Even if somebody had proposed something like that or if I had wanted to do it, there was no point after a month and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You knew of the phenomenon of the exchanges that were going on, the exchanges that were presided over by Mr. Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report on those?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Only in the news.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go down and have a look at the exchanges?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No, not as a rule.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you went and looked at some of the exchanges, at least?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to an exchange at a place called Sid on or about the 4th or 5th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. No, I really wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the exchanges that you did go to, from what you could see, was it your assessment that the people were being exchanged -- that the people who were being exchanged had no choice in the matter?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Well, these are questions which I can't really answer, and I have no reason to comment on them, because I publish what I hear and what I see and I do not go into any details, and that is a political issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just answer my question though. Is it your assessment that the people who were being exchanged had no choice in the matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Your Honours, that the first question was really speculative, and the witness already said that he couldn't answer that question and then he was asked the same thing once again, and it can be only his opinion whether he heard somebody say something or not, rather than whether in his assessment these people had any choice, because that is calling for speculation on his part. MR. DI FAZIO: No speculation is being called for. A very specific thing is being called for, his assessment. That's what's being called for. That's what the question suits, and it's that that I am seeking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is at the exchanges, if any, which he attended? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. He said he went to -- he went to some, and my question relates to the ones that he went to. I'm not asking him to speculate as to other exchanges at which he was not present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But his -- he can only give his assessment perhaps if -- he can't give his assessment because that amounts to opinion in accordance with what Mr. Lukic said. Did he hear anybody say anything about it? Did he ask the people who were being exchanged? MR. DI FAZIO: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the exchanges that you attended, did you see or hear anything that led you to the conclusion that people had no choice in their exchange?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. That is not my job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were reporting on news during 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever hear broadcast over the radio some piece of news or story to the effect that the paramilitaries Crni, Lugar, Laki, and others had been born in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I hope you are not repeating what you had asked before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Just a clarification of a couple of topics. Thank you. Further cross-examination by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antic, Simeon Simic told you that Simeon Simic and Todorovic would in future be in charge for the coordination in Radio Samac and so on and so forth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with reference to the sound engineer Pasaga Tihic. So if Stevan Todorovic was the chief of police and Pasaga Tihic was detained at his place, did you communicate with him, asking him to allow him to be incorporated in the work of Radio Samac? Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As an experienced -- as a seasoned journalist, would you please give us a brief assessment of the structure and work of Radio Samac in peacetime and in wartime. Is there a difference? And if there is, will you please explain it to us. In a nutshell what would it be?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Well, the difference is that in -- that you have peacetime programming and wartime programming. And in wartime programming, I always aspired to introduce something to provide the reporting for all peoples and to cover objectively insofar as possible and to report objectively, insofar as it was possible at that time. Of course, there were certain limitations. I've already told you why and how. And every news item had to be signed prior to the airing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And my last question: Since you were a member of the 4th Detachment, were you there as a professional, as a journalist, who would be responsible for propaganda in the 4th Detachment, because of your professionalism? Was that your special assignment?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: No, not as a special assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But basically that was your chief job, as a man who's a journalist?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there were -- there was responsibility for all areas, not for any specific detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But whatever, you promoted the objectives of the 4th Detachment, didn't you? I mean, the Yugoslav-hood and --

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Oh, that, yes. That, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time the SRK [as interpreted], movement for Yugoslavia, headed by General Mrkovic [phoen] and others, that was a topical party at the time which promoted Yugoslav-hood, a movement for Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: There was a lot of talk about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Antic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Page 116, line 10, instead of the abbreviation SRK, it should be SK-PJ, movement for Yugoslavia. That was the part of my question. Thank you. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Antic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. Re-examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antic, can you tell me, if you remember, who was the director of Radio Samac before the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Before the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Mato Krajinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did Mato Krajinovic come to be the director of Radio Samac?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mato Krajinovic a Croat?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went to that Radio Samac, were you put under labour [Realtime transcript read in error "legal"] obligation, were you issued with a decision?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, by the ministry -- by the department of the ministry, I can't remember what it was called. I had a decision in writing that I was being assigned to that job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that decision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My learned friend, Mr. Pisarevic, on page 117, line 6 asked: Were you put under work obligation, and in transcript there is a word "legal," so it should be corrected. Instead of "legal" it should be "work obligation." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That will be corrected. In fact, that's what I -- what I heard, that it was work obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. Before you move on, I wonder, Mr. Antic, whether you know what happened to your predecessor, Mato Krajinovic, the Croatian -- the Croat that you mentioned. Why -- do you know why he ceased to head up Radio Bosanski Samac at the time that you were put into that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your question. I really had no information about the whereabouts of Mato Krajinovic and why didn't he come to the station. I had no information whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree if I say that you were issued with the decision on the labour obligation, that is, work obligation, of the Ministry of National Defence Department of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right. Ministry for National Defence department in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, you were shown the statement, the proclamation of the 4th Detachment, and you told us today that that proclamation was read out by a presenter. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember whether the prohibition of access to Radio Samac for Mr. Zaric that was issued by Mr. Todorovic to you came after that proclamation was broadcast?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I have one question more: Your radio station where you were the editor-in-chief, was it a free radio station, or was it a radio which was subjected to the censorship by the authorities?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: It was a radio station which was subject to the censorship by the authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Antic, I just have one small question for you. Earlier on this afternoon, on page 83, lines 5 through 7 of the transcript, you were responding to a question put to you concerning any proclamation about the prohibition of the assembly of more than two or three Muslims or Croats in Samac. And you responded on lines 5 to 7 by saying that nothing had been broadcast to your knowledge but that you did read something about that on chestnut trees, that on the trunks there'd be such prohibitions, et cetera. And my question to you is: When you saw these pieces of paper on the chestnut trees, were they - how can I put it - official pieces of paper? Were they typed? Was there a stamp? Was there maybe a signature? Do you recall anything about what these posters looked like?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: They were typewritten, but I can't remember whether there were any signatures or stamps on them. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, I have a futile question but anyhow. As to active duty in the army, including the 4th Detachment, what was the upper age limit?

utterances.speaker: VASO ANTIC
utterances.text: I really don't know about others. I know that I was 55 at the time, so I suppose you can draw your own conclusions what was the age structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Antic. We are finished with your evidence. You may leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We've been informed that there are no witnesses. I just wanted to find out from Mr. Pantelic what the status is regarding his witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, thank you. I've been informed that in the next couple of days all witnesses will be in possession of new Bosnian passports, and thereafter in a couple of days they will obtain visa through Witness and Victims Unit, so they will be ready to come here the first working day, which is the 28th of April, I believe. And the court officer is fully informed through various channels, including the main channel, which is Victims and Witness Unit two witnesses for your information -- probably you were informed, but I can tell you that two witnesses were yesterday on the border between Bosnia and Serbia, waiting for the final approval of the Dutch embassy in Belgrade through Dutch Ministry for Foreign Affairs. But unfortunately due to some administrative problems they didn't obtain that approval and they were back by the transportation unit of Victims and Witnesses Unit to Samac. So they were on the way to The Hague, but unfortunately due to some reasons beyond our control they were not able to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for the information. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if there are no other issues to discuss, I'd like to say only two words for the record. I know that the interpreters must also be tired, but I think it is very important. It has to do with our demographic expert analysis. As you know, our demographic expert has arrived and is really cooperating well with the Prosecutor's Office, and what is most important for us, they will complete their work by tomorrow noon. I've just talked to them. However, there is a problem which I believe is of technical nature and I will try to explain it, although I am a layman, and why does it matter? Namely, as they are searching, they are not allowed to record any of this material. And of course you understand this, because this material we understand is classified and the -- and international organisations and governments have allowed them to search through them. But when they complete their work, they will then have to work, as I presume the OTP did, they have to use a particular computer programme. However, this computer programme which will serve as a basis for their expert opinion is the only document, the only evidence to show how they came by those results. I have already informed Mr. Di Fazio that we are suggesting to them that that programme which they are not allowed to tape - and the OTP knows it - that in case that there is cross-examination or the verification of the conclusions of our experts, we think that this programme should be recorded and then filed with the registry, because that will be the only way in which our witness will be able to document his results. I've already explained it to Mr. Di Fazio, and he has agreed in principle. So when they finish with their analysis tomorrow afternoon, then that programme which they are using as a basis which underpins their investigation, all this should be stored with the registry so that if necessary it -- this programme could be used in the possible cross-examination later on so that our expert could refer simply to it to show what he had done. That is, it will serve as evidence, as proof, which allowed him to draw his expert conclusions. So what we are asking is that this document, this programme which is on -- on a disk, on a floppy disk, that it be stored with the registry so that it could be used later if need be and so that the witness could refer to it again if necessary in his testimony. I've already told Mr. Di Fazio, and he's agreed, but I wanted to raise this because if this programme is destroyed later on and he cannot use it in his testimony, in case of necessity then we shall be in trouble. So that is my proposal, for this floppy disk to be kept with the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to confirm with the Prosecution that is -- that has been discussed and agreed. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, that's been discussed and agreed. And it's a good idea that the evidence -- that that particular disk be preserved somewhere safe. And I have no problem with that at all. The only thing I'm -- and I'm also quite happy for it to be kept with the registry. In fact, from the Prosecution's point of view that's probably a good solution to the situation. I assume that there'll be no problem from registry from that. And if that's all okay, then as soon as the disk has been finished with, I'll take it and I'll hand it to an official at the registry and ask them to keep it at hand until the end of the trial so that we -- we can -- it's available to be used if and when needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And if I may add, Your Honour, with regard to the same issue, this disk should be sealed in some kind of bag, according to the standard of keeping the evidence, signed by the people who are in charge, stamped or whatever. I don't know what the standard is, but I'm sure that the registry will take care about that, that it will be proper in accordance with the legal standards. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Of course. They always do that with any piece of evidence that is required for -- in any of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've got one last matter, just very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One quick -- one last matter which will be very brief. The Prosecution was given until tomorrow to respond to Mr. Pantelic's attempt to proffer a large number of documents, a report plus a large number of documents from a General or Colonel Wilmont, a military expert. Since we were initially given a group of -- we were initially given the report then we received one group of documents and then after we were given this date tomorrow we received another group of documents. We've compiled now three binders of documents which are right over here and in addition we've obtained the transcripts he's testified for two days in the Stakic case and we need another week to review everything before we can make a decision. We're requesting an additional week from the Court or that we report on the first day of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber was informed and they -- with regard also, there are also other matters which the Trial Chamber wants to deal with. And we shall sit on Thursday at 9.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. On the request of the Prosecution regarding the Wilmont opinion, that is fine. The Trial Chamber is prepared to give them one week. We shall rise now, and we will sit on Thursday at 9.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: at 3.38 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of April, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
